title: The theorem of the cube over a field
statement:
Let $k$ be a field and let $X$, $Y$, $Z$ be schemes over $k$ [def-weil-scheme-over-base]. Assume $X$ and $Y$ are proper over $k$ [def-weil-proper-morphism] and geometrically integral over $k$ [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], and let $x$, $y$ be $k$-rational points of $X$, $Y$ [def-pc-rational-point]. Assume $Z$ is connected [def-weil-connected-scheme]. Let $\mathcal L$ be an invertible module [def-sc-invertible-module] on the fibre product $X\times_kY\times_kZ$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. If
(1) the pullbacks [def-pc-module-pullback] of $\mathcal L$ along $x\times\mathrm{id}_Y\times\mathrm{id}_Z:Y\times_kZ\to X\times_kY\times_kZ$ and along $\mathrm{id}_X\times y\times\mathrm{id}_Z:X\times_kZ\to X\times_kY\times_kZ$ are trivial (isomorphic to the structure sheaf), and
(2) there is a point $z\in Z$, with residue field $\kappa(z)$ [def-weil-residue-field], such that the pullback of $\mathcal L$ to the fibre $X\times_kY\times_k\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(z)$ [def-pc-base-change] is trivial,
then $\mathcal L\cong\mathcal O_{X\times_kY\times_kZ}$.

source.place: More on Morphisms, Theorem 37.33.8, Tag 0BF4 (more-morphisms-theorem-of-the-cube), specialised to S = Spec k, where proper morphisms are flat and of finite presentation

proof.text: Let $p:X\times_kY\times_kZ\to Z$ be the projection. Properness and finite presentation are stable under products and base change, and flatness over the field $k$ is automatic. By Varieties, Lemmas 038K, 038F and 035Z, after any field extension the product of the geometrically integral base changes of $X$ and $Y$ is geometrically integral; hence $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, $X\times_kY\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ and their base changes to $Z$ (in particular $p$) have geometrically integral fibres, in particular geometrically reduced and connected.

source.place: More on Morphisms, Theorem 37.33.8 proof, lines 9684-9689; Varieties product lemmas

proof.text: Applying Tag 0E0L to $X\times_kY\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ and then base changing to $Z$ gives $p_*\mathcal O_{X\times_kY\times_kZ}=\mathcal O_Z$, universally. Likewise Tag 0E0L applied to $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ shows that $X\times_kZ\to Z$ and $Y\times_kZ\to Z$ have $\mathcal O_T\to(\cdot)_*\mathcal O$ an isomorphism after every base change $T\to Z$.

source.place: More on Morphisms, proof of Theorem 37.33.8, Tag 0E0L

proof.text: By Tag 0BDP applied to $p$ and $\mathcal L$, there is a universal locally closed subscheme $Z'\subset Z$ and an invertible module $\mathcal N$ on $Z'$ such that the restriction of $\mathcal L$ to $X\times_kY\times_kZ'$ is $p^*\mathcal N$.

source.place: More on Morphisms, proof of Theorem 37.33.8, Tag 0BDP

proof.text: The assumed triviality on the fibre over $z$ means that $z$ factors through $Z'$, so $Z'$ is nonempty.

source.place: More on Morphisms, proof of Theorem 37.33.8, after Tag 0BDP

proof.text: Since the fibres of $p$ are geometrically integral, Tag 0BF0 applied to the same universal locus shows that $Z'$ is closed in $Z$.

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma get-a-closed, Tag 0BF0

proof.text: Choose a point $z'\in Z'$. Write $p$ as $(X\times_k Z)\times_Z(Y\times_k Z)\to Z$, a product of two flat, proper morphisms of finite presentation satisfying the universal pushforward condition (Step 2), with sections $\sigma:Z\to X\times_kZ$ and $\tau:Z\to Y\times_kZ$ induced by $x$ and $y$. The pullbacks $(1\times\tau)^*\mathcal L$ and $(\sigma\times1)^*\mathcal L$ are the pullbacks along $\mathrm{id}_X\times y\times\mathrm{id}_Z$ and $x\times\mathrm{id}_Y\times\mathrm{id}_Z$, trivial by hypothesis (1), and the restriction of $\mathcal L$ to the fibre over $z'$ is trivial because $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(z')\to Z$ factors through the universal locus $Z'$ and every invertible module on $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(z')$ is free. Tag 0BF3 therefore gives an open neighbourhood $U$ of $z'$ such that $\mathcal L$ is trivial on $p^{-1}(U)$. By the universal factorization property of $Z'$ (with $\mathcal N=\mathcal O_U$), the inclusion $U\to Z$ factors through $Z'$, so $Z'$ contains an open neighbourhood of each of its points and is open in $Z$.

source.place: More on Morphisms, proof of Theorem 37.33.8, lines 9704-9711; Tag 0BF3

proof.text: Thus the image of $Z'\to Z$ is nonempty (Step 4), closed (Step 5) and open (Step 6) in the connected scheme $Z$, hence equal to $Z$. The open sets $U$ of Step 6 then cover $Z$ and each inclusion $U\to Z$ factors through the immersion $Z'\to Z$, which is a monomorphism; so these factorizations glue and $\mathrm{id}_Z$ factors through $Z'$, i.e. $Z'=Z$.

source.place: More on Morphisms, proof of Theorem 37.33.8, connectedness conclusion

proof.text: We have $\mathcal L\cong p^*\mathcal N$ on all of $X\times_kY\times_kZ$. Pulling back along $x\times y\times\mathrm{id}_Z$ identifies $\mathcal N$ with the pullback of $\mathcal L$ along that slice, which is trivial by (1); hence $\mathcal N\cong\mathcal O_Z$ and $\mathcal L\cong\mathcal O_{X\times_kY\times_kZ}$.

source.place: More on Morphisms, proof of Theorem 37.33.8, final paragraph

lean.statement: theorem nonempty_iso_unit_of_tensorPullback_slices_and_fiber {k : Type u} [Field k] (X Y Z : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper X.hom] [GeometricallyIntegral X.hom] [IsProper Y.hom] [GeometricallyIntegral Y.hom] [ConnectedSpace Z.left] (x : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ X) (y : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ Y) (L : ((X ⊗ Y) ⊗ Z).left.Modules) [L.IsInvertible] (hx : Nonempty ((Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback (lift (lift (toUnit (Y ⊗ Z) ≫ x) (fst Y Z)) (snd Y Z)).left).obj L ≅ SheafOfModules.unit _)) (hy : Nonempty ((Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback (lift (lift (fst X Z) (toUnit (X ⊗ Z) ≫ y)) (snd X Z)).left).obj L ≅ SheafOfModules.unit _)) (hz : ∃ z : Z.left, Nonempty ((Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback ((snd (X ⊗ Y) Z).left.fiberι z)).obj L ≅ SheafOfModules.unit _)) : Nonempty (L ≅ SheafOfModules.unit _)
